elements.title: Two-qubit logic and teleportation with mobile spin qubits in silicon (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Two-qubit logic and teleportation with mobile spin qubits in silicon

A device architecture comprising silicon-based mobile qubits and the shuttling of two electron spins together demonstrates two-qubit gate fidelity of about 99% as well as quantum state teleportation between qubits separated by 320 nm.

  • Y. Matsumoto
  • M. De Smet
  • L. M. K. Vandersypen
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Expanding the human proteome with microproteins and peptideins (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Expanding the human proteome with microproteins and peptideins

A large-scale proteomics analysis of the dark proteome by the TransCODE Consortium reveals many translated non-canonical open reading frames to encode microproteins and peptideins.

  • Eric W. Deutsch
  • Leron W. Kok
  • Sebastiaan van Heesch
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: RNA-triggered cell killing with CRISPR–Cas12a2 (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
RNA-triggered cell killing with CRISPR–Cas12a2

Cas12a2 enables RNA-triggered, sequence-specific killing of eukaryotic cells via widespread DNA shredding, allowing selective elimination of cells on the basis of gene expression, including virus-infected or mutation-bearing cells.

  • Paul Scholz
  • Jared Thompson
  • Yang Liu
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Pollinators support the nutrition and income of vulnerable communities (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Pollinators support the nutrition and income of vulnerable communities

Quantification of links among insect pollinators, crop plants, nutrient intake and income of smallholder communities in Nepal show that pollinators substantially contribute to their income and micronutrient intake.

  • T. P. Timberlake
  • S. Sapkota
  • J. Memmott
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Electrocaloric effects across room temperature in multilayer capacitors (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Electrocaloric effects across room temperature in multilayer capacitors

Multilayer capacitors comprising a solid solution of two electrocaloric materials PbSc0.5Ta0.5O3 and PbMg0.5W0.5O3 are shown to maintain high B-site order and latent heat without needing an energetically expensive anneal, enabling efficient refrigeration across room temperature.

  • M. Guo
  • V. Farenkov
  • N. D. Mathur
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Foreshock-induced slip transients set mainshock nucleation timing (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Foreshock-induced slip transients set mainshock nucleation timing

Analysis of laboratory experiments using a rate-and-state-based Griffith-like rupture framework shows that foreshocks can regulate mainshock nucleation timing, with larger foreshocks generating higher transient sliding velocities and triggering a more rapid transition to dynamic rupture.

  • Barnaby Fryer
  • Dmitry Garagash
  • François Passelègue
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Non-invasive profiling of the tumour microenvironment with spatial ecotypes (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Non-invasive profiling of the tumour microenvironment with spatial ecotypes

Multimodal machine learning reveals that tumour microenvironments can be decomposed into spatially organized multicellular ecosystems, termed spatial ecotypes, that can be accessed non-invasively via liquid biopsy and used to profile individual cancers and target treatments.

  • Wubing Zhang
  • Erin L. Brown
  • Aaron M. Newman
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Plasticity and language in the anaesthetized human hippocampus (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Plasticity and language in the anaesthetized human hippocampus

In the hippocampus, complex processing of sensory stimuli occurs even in the unconscious state.

  • Kalman A. Katlowitz
  • Eric R. Cole
  • Sameer A. Sheth
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Genome-wide sweeps create ecological units in the human gut microbiome (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Genome-wide sweeps create ecological units in the human gut microbiome

Genome-wide selective sweeps commonly occur in the human gut microbiome and can spread across the world within decades to produce epidemic-like population structures.

  • Xiaoqian Annie Yu
  • Cameron R. Strachan
  • Martin F. Polz
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Tree community resource economics control soil food web multifunctionality (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Tree community resource economics control soil food web multifunctionality

Plant community properties affect ecosystem functioning via energy fluxes in food webs, with the leaf and root resource economics of dominant tree species controlling soil food web multifunctionality.

  • Ludovic Henneron
  • David A. Wardle
  • Paul Kardol
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Prefrontal to ventral tegmental area dynamics drive contingency degradation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Prefrontal to ventral tegmental area dynamics drive contingency degradation

This work provides a mechanistic understanding of how certain prefrontal circuits in the rodent brain permit flexibility to selectively stop learned behaviours through interactions with core subcortical reward systems.

  • Madelyn M. Hjort
  • Zoe Q. Garrett
  • Garret D. Stuber
Article06 May 2026

elements.title: Steric hindrance of antibody binding in an Omicron spike fusion intermediate (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Steric hindrance of antibody binding in an Omicron spike fusion intermediate

The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant escapes neutralization by antibodies targeting the pan-coronavirus epitope in a spike fusion intermediate via steric hindrance, but reducing the antibody size overcomes this barrier and expands its range of accessible targets.

  • Zhiheng Bao
  • Zhimin Liu
  • Xiaoyu Sun
Article06 May 2026

elements.title: Purcell-enhanced spin–phonon coupling with a single colour centre (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Purcell-enhanced spin–phonon coupling with a single colour centre

The acoustic Purcell effect is observed by constructing a specially engineered, microwave-frequency nanomechanical resonator around a colour centre spin qubit in diamond.

  • Graham Joe
  • Michael Haas
  • Marko Lončar
Article06 May 2026

elements.title: Predicting temporal stability and resilience from resistance and recovery (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Predicting temporal stability and resilience from resistance and recovery

New predictions for how temporal stability and resilience depend on their resistance and recovery components are explored.

  • Forest Isbell
  • Akira S. Mori
  • Chad R. Zirbel
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: HIV-1 signalling remodels nuclear pores to licence infection (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
HIV-1 signalling remodels nuclear pores to licence infection

HIV-1 capsid nuclear import at the nuclear pore complex is a bottleneck to resting T cell infection, but HIV-1 overcomes this by triggering receptor-mediated signalling during cell–cell spread to drive nuclear import and licence infection.

  • Dejan Mesner
  • Matthew V. X. Whelan
  • Clare Jolly
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Specific expansion of motor cortical projections in a singing mouse (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Specific expansion of motor cortical projections in a singing mouse

High-throughput barcoded neuroanatomy of two closely related rodent species with divergent vocalizations reveals differences in long-range projection motifs in the brain that may support these differences in vocal complexity.

  • Emily C. Isko
  • Clifford E. Harpole
  • Arkarup Banerjee
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Quantum coherent manipulation and readout of superconducting vortex states (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Quantum coherent manipulation and readout of superconducting vortex states

Vortices trapped in superconducting granular aluminium films can behave as a quantum two-level system that can be manipulated and read out, suggesting that they could be used for future quantum technologies.

  • Ameya Nambisan
  • Simon Günzler
  • Ioan M. Pop
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Imaging the flat bands of magic-angle graphene reshaped by interactions (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Imaging the flat bands of magic-angle graphene reshaped by interactions

Quantum twisting microscopy is used to directly image the interacting energy bands of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, allowing characterization of the dual nature of its electrons at the magic angle.

  • J. Xiao
  • A. Inbar
  • S. Ilani
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Deforestation-induced drying lowers Amazon climate threshold (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Deforestation-induced drying lowers Amazon climate threshold

The Amazon forest faces a near system-wide transition of 62−77% of the area under a combination of 1.5–1.9 °C global warming and 22−28% deforestation.

  • Nico Wunderling
  • Boris Sakschewski
  • Arie Staal
ArticleOpen Access06 May 2026

elements.title: Molecular skeleton programming of premediators in sulfur electrochemistry (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Molecular skeleton programming of premediators in sulfur electrochemistry

A potential premediator, 2-chloropyrimidine, could be a model material for molecular skeleton design enabling lithium–sulfur batteries to achieve a strong average capacity retention and help design functional molecules in broader organic chemical spaces.

  • Runhua Gao
  • Yifei Zhu
  • Guangmin Zhou
Article06 May 2026
